title: The Golden Spoon in the Emperor's Bowl (PT)
summary: Akbar boasts that eating with golden cutlery makes common food taste celestial. Birbal shows the Emperor that true taste resides in hunger.
full_text:
The imperial treasury received a shipment of exquisite solid gold spoons, forks, and bowls encrusted with sapphires from the goldsmiths of Gujarat. Eating his dinner that evening, Emperor Akbar remarked to Birbal:

'Look at this golden spoon, Birbal! It is so smooth, so pure, and so radiant! Truly, eating with gold elevates the food itself; even common lentil broth tastes like divine nectar when spooned from gold!'

Birbal smiled gently: 'Sire, gold is a cold, tasteless metal. It cannot add a single drop of sweetness to sour food, nor can it nourish a hungry stomach. The flavor of food is created by the tongue of hunger, not by the metal of the spoon.'

Akbar scoffed: 'Are you claiming that a wooden spoon is equal to an imperial golden spoon?'

'Let us test the truth tomorrow, Your Majesty,' Birbal suggested.

The next day, Birbal invited Akbar to go hunting in the rocky, barren ravines of Chambal. Birbal deliberately led the royal party deep into the labyrinth of hills, taking four hours of strenuous riding beneath a blistering sun.

By late afternoon, Akbar was parched with thirst and ravenous with hunger, his stomach rumbling painfully.

Birbal stopped near the stone hut of an impoverished goatherd. The goatherd had only a pot of cold, sour millet porridge and a few raw onions, served in a cracked clay bowl with a rough wooden spoon carved from a neem branch.

Akbar did not ask for gold. He grabbed the wooden spoon, devoured the bitter porridge and raw onions with ferocious delight, and drank two bowls of cold well water, sighing in bliss:

'By Allah, Birbal! That was the most delicious, savory feast I have tasted in my entire life! What spices did the goatherd use?'

Birbal laughed softly:

'Sire, the goatherd used no spices, and your spoon was rough neem wood!

'The spice that made the food heavenly was five hours of honest hunger! A hungry man finds sweet ambrosia in cold porridge eaten with a wooden spoon, while a pampered, bloated emperor finds even roasted pheasant tasteless upon a golden plate!

'Luxury resides in the utensil, but true satisfaction resides in the healthy hunger of the body.'

Akbar smiled warmly and rewarded the goatherd, acknowledging that Birbal's wisdom had once again pierced through royal vanity.
moral: Lição de moral: Wit beats power
